notes: בְּיוֹם הִמָּשַׁח אֹתוֹ follows rule 52's last clause: in goes to the preposition, the day to the construct, and when he is anointed to the infinitive with its suffix taking the passive subject pronoun.
The two halves are rendered differently by the ASV (of it, thereof); each suffix takes what is written for it.

In the tenth part of an ephah the article on הָאֵיפָה stays unrepresented and the construct takes a supplied the: rule 29's fronting is what an anarthrous rendering of the rectum forces, and here the ASV writes a positive an before ephah.
